raw_response:
I’m 51 this year, and with only 5 mu, I can’t take big risks. I’ve farmed here in Quzhou a long time, so I mostly follow what has worked on my own land and what I see nearby. Cotton gives cash, but it ties up the land the whole year and needs more careful picking and pest watching. Wheat and maize together are steadier. Even if one side is not great, the other can make up some. Since my family only has 2 people and some off-farm work, I can’t spread myself too thin. So this year I’ll keep most of the land in cotton, because that is my main system, but I’ll still keep a small piece in wheat and then summer maize, just so I have some grain and don’t put everything on one crop.

For cotton, I’ll use the better 3 mu and plant in mid-late April after the soil warms up. I won’t go too heavy on fertilizer because money is tight, but I also can’t be too stingy or the plants stay weak. I’ll put most fertilizer as base, then one more topdressing when squaring starts. Cotton needs watching for insects, so I’ll spray only if I really see trouble. For the 2 mu grain land, I’ll sow wheat in early October and harvest in early June, then rush to plant summer maize right after. That piece has a tight turnaround, so I’ll do simple rotary tillage and not waste time. Wheat gets a bit more water because one irrigation at jointing usually pays back. Maize I’ll keep simpler, with one base fertilizer and maybe one watering if summer rain is poor. I’m not chasing the highest yield. I just want a stable year without spending too much cash up front.
